neighbours.label: The token ' quite' (lowercase, leading space) when the nearest preceding content word is a lexical verb or the verb's object noun/pronoun; near-zero when a finite copula (is/was/are) or 'not' stands within two tokens before it, and for degree synonyms (rather, fairly, very) in the same slot.
fire: Over the past decade the village has grown quite noticeably, with new houses along the ridge.
When the lights dimmed, the audience settled quite quickly and the first act began.
Since the merger, the bank has handled customer complaints quite differently.
By the third week the seedlings in the greenhouse had spread quite vigorously.
During the drought the price of hay climbed quite steeply across the region.
The old mill wheel still turns, though the stream that drives it has narrowed quite dramatically.
Even without a map, the scouts found the trail quite easily and reached camp before dark.
In her second season the young pitcher controlled her fastball quite well, striking out ten.
quiet: By the end of the drought the water in the village reservoir was quite low for the season.
The new hiking trails above the village are quite steep in places.
The seedlings in the greenhouse had not quite reached the top of the frame by June.
Under the new manager the bank has handled customer complaints rather differently.
During the dry summer the price of feed climbed fairly steeply across the valley.
Once the curtain rose, the crowd settled very quickly and the play began.
As the house lights faded, the audience went quiet and the overture began.
The scouts (quite literally) stumbled onto the trail back to camp before dark.
